name: Battle of Salamis

sides.name: Greek allied fleet
sides.strength: About 370 to 380 triremes drawn from Athens, Corinth, Aegina, and the wider Hellenic alliance

sides.name: Achaemenid Persia
sides.commander: Xerxes I (overall), Achaemenes and Ariabignes (squadron commanders)
sides.strength: Roughly 600 to 800 triremes drawn from Phoenicia, Egypt, Ionia, and the wider empire
sides.casualties: Around 200 to 300 triremes destroyed or captured

summary: Themistocles lured the Persian fleet into the narrow strait between Salamis and the Athenian mainland with a fake message about Greek treachery. In the confined channel the larger Persian fleet lost its numerical advantage. Ships fouled each other while Greek triremes rammed and boarded them in detail. Xerxes watched the destruction from his throne on the slopes of Mount Aigaleo and withdrew the bulk of his army to Asia, leaving his commander Mardonius to winter in Greece.
significance: Salamis broke the strategic momentum of the Persian invasion. Without naval superiority Xerxes could no longer keep his enormous army supplied. The following spring Mardonius's army was destroyed at Plataea and the Greek allies took the offensive into the Aegean. Themistocles's victory established Athenian naval power, which underwrote the fifth-century empire and the cultural flowering that produced classical Athens.
